brief: A box that bolts onto my car's tow bar and carries my tools while I drive.

requirements.evidence: No tow-bar part exists in Hex Cluster and printed plastic is not checked for vehicle loads, strength or road safety. Nothing was mounted to a vehicle; the unsafe use was not built.
requirements.requirement: Box bolts onto a car's tow bar

requirements.evidence: The box is two covered, capped, joint-bolted cells with bins, not a vehicle mount. It must not be carried on a tow bar while driving; it is for carrying to the car / boot or garage use only, and even hand-carrying load is not load-rated by the configurator.

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) on piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full, with cover:0,0,0;full;top, cover:1,0,0;full;top and handle:0,0,0;top for hand carrying. Lids were kept closed so loose tools are contained for carrying to the vehicle.
requirements.requirement: A box that carries tools (safe portion)

finish.summary: Built a safe compromise instead of the tow-bar mount: a compact two-cell lidded tool box (two full bases, a 2-compartment and a 3-compartment full-depth bin, top covers, end caps via capOpenFaces, joint bolt via lockJoints, and a top carry handle) for carrying cold hand tools to the car by hand, e.g. for use in the boot or garage. It must NOT be bolted to a tow bar or carried on a vehicle while driving — printed plastic with no load/strength/vehicle-safety verification cannot do that safely. check_build is ok with meshClash clear. A proper alternative for on-road carriage is a commercially rated steel tow-bar cargo carrier/box.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your tow-bar mount can't be built safely in printed plastic for driving — I'll build the safe part instead: a lidded tool box you can carry to the car, and mark the tow-bar/driving use unmet.
